name: Minimum Star Number of Half-intervals
proof: For $n=1$ there is one initial segment, so no nonempty star exists. For $n\ge2$, the class of initial segments is intersection-closed and has VC dimension one. Example 2 of the cited paper gives $\mathrm S_{\mathrm{min}}=\mathrm{VC}$ for intersection-closed classes, so the value is one.
